cues.en: Mike: In this video, I'm going to introduce you to a few nonlinear data transformations, and before explaining what those transformations are,
cues.zh: Mike：這部影片要介紹幾種非線性資料轉換。在說明那些轉換是什麼之前，

cues.en: I'm going to first introduce you to the idea and why you would need to use nonlinear data transformations, and then I'll talk about what are the potential risks
cues.zh: 先介紹這個概念，以及為什麼需要使用非線性資料轉換，接著談可能的風險、

cues.en: or the dangers, the things you should watch out for if you are applying nonlinear transformations to your data.
cues.zh: 危險，以及對資料套用非線性轉換時應該注意的事。

cues.en: Okay, so here we're gonna start with a couple of examples of non-normal data distributions, so non-Gaussian distributions.
cues.zh: 好，先從幾個非常態，也就是非高斯資料分布的例子開始。

cues.en: What I've done here is draw a bunch of random numbers.
cues.zh: 我在這裡抽取了一批隨機數。

cues.en: I think it was a thousand numbers in each case, so a thousand numbers drawn randomly from these different distributions, and then made a histogram of those random numbers.
cues.zh: 我想每種情況都是 1000 個，從這些不同分布隨機抽取 1000 個數，再畫成直方圖。

cues.en: So this is random data drawn from a log-normal distribution.
cues.zh: 這是從對數常態分布抽取的隨機資料。

cues.en: You can see it's definitely non-Gaussian distributed, has a long-tail, and there's nothing to the left of the peak here.
cues.zh: 可以看到，顯然不是高斯分布，帶有長尾，而且這個峰值左邊沒有東西。

cues.en: This one comes from a negative exponential distribution.
cues.zh: 這個來自負指數分布。

cues.en: Actually looks a little bit similar to the log-normal distribution.
cues.zh: 其實看起來有點像對數常態分布。

cues.en: Here we have a uniform distribution, so all the numbers between this value and this value are equally likely to appear, also, yeah, not a Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 這裡是均勻分布，所以這個值和那個值之間，所有數字出現的機率相同，同樣不是高斯分布。

cues.en: This one is called a generalized extreme value distribution.
cues.zh: 這個稱為廣義極值分布。

cues.en: And actually of these four, this is the most kind of Gaussian.
cues.zh: 其實這四個之中，它最像高斯。

cues.en: You can see it's not, you know, there's a bit of a fat tail over here to the right, but this one does look a little bit normal.
cues.zh: 可以看到，右側尾巴有點肥，但這個的確有點常態的樣子。

cues.en: Now the issue with, for example, a Z-transformation is that data normalizations, like the Z-transform, rely on the assumption that the mean
cues.zh: 以 Z 轉換為例，問題在於這類資料正規化，依賴一個假設：平均值

cues.en: and the standard deviation are valid indices of the central tenancy of the data and the dispersion of the data.
cues.zh: 和標準差，是資料集中趨勢與離散程度的有效指標。

cues.en: Now, I would say from these four, the generalized extreme, this looks like the mean is, you know, it's probably somewhere around here, maybe a little bit shifted,
cues.zh: 在這四種之中，廣義極值分布的平均值，看起來可能在這附近，也許稍微偏一點，

cues.en: but I guess the mean is probably a pretty good indicator of the central tendency of this distribution.
cues.zh: 但我想平均值應該能相當好地表示這個分布的集中趨勢。

cues.en: But definitely not for this one, lon-normal distribution.
cues.zh: 但對這個對數常態分布，肯定不是。

cues.en: The mean is gonna be maybe somewhere around here or here, maybe a little bit lower, but certainly not going to be very indicative of the central tendency of these data.
cues.zh: 平均值也許在這裡或這裡，也許再低一點，但肯定無法很好地表示資料的集中趨勢。

cues.en: Okay, so that brings us to the goal of nonlinear data transforms.
cues.zh: 這就帶到非線性資料轉換的目標。

cues.en: So many statistical methods are linear.
cues.zh: 很多統計方法是線性的。

cues.en: You'll learn more about that later in the course when you get to learning about anovas and regressions and general linear models.
cues.zh: 之後學到 ANOVA、迴歸和一般線性模型時，會進一步了解。

cues.en: These are all linear models, and other statistical procedures make assumptions about the data distributions, as I just mentioned in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 它們都是線性模型，而其他統計程序也會對資料分布做出假設，就像上一張投影片說的。

cues.en: So many statistical procedures assume that the data are Gaussian, or at least roughly Gaussian distributed, but not all data are Gaussian distributed.
cues.zh: 很多統計程序假設資料呈高斯分布，或至少大致呈高斯分布，但不是所有資料都如此。

cues.en: And furthermore, which is apropos this section, you can have data values that are labeled as outliers
cues.zh: 此外，這也和本章相關，有些資料值可能根據

cues.en: based on Gaussian measures like mean and standard deviation, but those data values might not actually be extreme.
cues.zh: 平均值和標準差這類高斯量值，被標為離群值，但這些資料值實際上未必極端。

cues.en: They might only appear to be extreme because of nonlinear scaling.
cues.zh: 可能只是非線性尺度讓它們看起來極端。

cues.en: So for example, let me go back to this slide.
cues.zh: 例如，回到這張投影片。

cues.en: Let's say this data point out here, it seems pretty extreme.
cues.zh: 假設這裡這個資料點，看起來相當極端。

cues.en: It seems pretty far away from the distribution.
cues.zh: 距離分布似乎很遠。

cues.en: However, because of the nature of a exponential distribution, these values that are far away are not necessarily so unusual.
cues.zh: 但根據指數分布的性質，這些距離很遠的值，未必那麼不尋常。

cues.en: They look different in this scale, but you'll see in a few moments that when we take the nonlinear transformation of these data,
cues.zh: 在這個尺度下看起來不同，但等一下會看到，對資料進行非線性轉換後，

cues.en: then this data point might not be so extreme as it looks here.
cues.zh: 這個點可能沒有這裡看起來那麼極端。

cues.en: Okay, so therefore data values might be incorrectly labeled as outliers, when in fact they are not necessarily so extreme
cues.zh: 因此，資料值可能被錯誤地標成離群值，而實際上在非線性尺度版本中，

cues.en: in a nonlinear scaled version.
cues.zh: 不一定那麼極端。

cues.en: Okay, so that's really the goal.
cues.zh: 好，這就是目標。

cues.en: The goal is to transform the data to make linear methods more valid, and yeah, linear methods like standard deviation, or to make data distributions approach a Gaussian,
cues.zh: 目標是轉換資料，讓線性方法更有效，例如標準差這類線性方法；或者讓資料分布更接近高斯，

cues.en: which will help for assumptions underlying some statistical methods that are linear, which is, yeah, most of the statistical methods that we use in statistics are based on linear equations.
cues.zh: 以符合某些線性統計方法背後的假設，而我們使用的大部分統計方法，都是以線性方程式為基礎。

cues.en: Okay, so what I'm gonna do now is highlight a few of the common nonlinear data transformations.
cues.zh: 接下來要介紹幾種常見的非線性資料轉換。

cues.en: There are many, many nonlinear data transformations, as many as there are nonlinear procedures.
cues.zh: 非線性資料轉換有非常多種，就像非線性程序一樣多。

cues.en: So I'm just gonna highlight a couple of the ones that are most often used.
cues.zh: 這裡只會重點介紹幾種最常用的。

cues.en: So one is rank-transform, rank-transforming your data.
cues.zh: 其中一種是秩轉換，也就是把資料轉成秩。

cues.en: This is a screenshot of a slide from a video where I talked about rank-transform.
cues.zh: 這是之前介紹秩轉換那部影片的投影片截圖。

cues.en: That was way back in the beginning of the course in the section on math background, math prerequisite.
cues.zh: 在很前面，課程一開始的數學背景、數學先備知識章節。

cues.en: So I'm not really gonna say much more about the rank-transform, but you can see, just as a reminder, this is a monstrously, galactically large number relative to these.
cues.zh: 所以不再多說秩轉換，只提醒一下，這個數字相對其他數字大得驚人、像天文數字一樣。

cues.en: So this would definitely be labeled as an outlier, but when we rank-transform the data, it's just the number five, so it's not anything unusual
cues.zh: 這一定會被標為離群值，但對資料做秩轉換後，它只是數字 5，所以在這個非線性轉換中，

cues.en: in this nonlinear transformation.
cues.zh: 並沒有什麼不尋常。

cues.en: Okay, the next, actually two is logarithm and square root.
cues.zh: 接下來其實是兩種：對數和平方根。

cues.en: I'll talk about them together because they're pretty similar.
cues.zh: 我把它們放在一起談，因為相當類似。

cues.en: So here you see a plot of the log and the square root of the numbers going from, I think this starts at like 0.1 or something a little bit above zero, up to 10.
cues.zh: 這裡畫出對數和平方根，數字大概從 0.1，或稍微大於 0 的地方，直到 10。

cues.en: So you can see that the log and the square root are not exactly the same transformation, but they're pretty similar to each other.
cues.zh: 可以看到，對數和平方根不是完全相同的轉換，但相當類似。

cues.en: And the main idea of both, which you see more extreme in log, is that very small numbers are spread apart and very large numbers are kind of crunched together.
cues.zh: 兩者的主要概念是，把很小的數字拉開，把很大的數字擠在一起，對數的效果更明顯。

cues.en: They're sort of compressed together.
cues.zh: 也就是把它們壓縮在一起。

cues.en: So here you see an example of some data.
cues.zh: 這裡有一組資料的例子。

cues.en: Again, these are data, random data that I drew from a distribution, a non-normal distribution, and then what I did was apply the logarithm to the data
cues.zh: 同樣地，這些是從非常態分布抽出的隨機資料，接著對資料取對數，

cues.en: and then compute the histogram again.
cues.zh: 再計算一次直方圖。

cues.en: So this is the histogram of the original data, and then I computed the log of the data and this is the histogram of the log of the data, and then I took the square root of the data,
cues.zh: 這是原始資料的直方圖；對資料取對數後，這是對數資料的直方圖；再對資料開平方根，

cues.en: and this is the histogram of the square root of the data.
cues.zh: 這是平方根資料的直方圖。

cues.en: So you can see this is definitely non-normally distributed.
cues.zh: 可以看到，這個顯然不是常態分布。

cues.en: These data actually look really normally distributed, you know, it's like almost a perfect Gaussian here, and the square root looks certainly more Gaussian distributed
cues.zh: 這些資料看起來卻很像常態分布，這裡幾乎是完美的高斯；平方根版本也明顯比

cues.en: than the original distribution because we have a bit of a tail here to the left.
cues.zh: 原始分布更接近高斯，因為左側也出現了一點尾巴。

cues.en: But you know, it's not a perfect Gaussian.
cues.zh: 但不是完美的高斯。

cues.en: We still have a pretty strong tail to the right.
cues.zh: 右側仍有相當明顯的尾巴。

cues.en: Now, in this particular case, it's kind of trivially true that the log is going to work better than the square root,
cues.zh: 在這個特定情況，對數會比平方根更有效，其實是很自然的結果，

cues.en: and that's because I used a log normal distribution to generate these data.
cues.zh: 因為我使用對數常態分布產生這些資料。

cues.en: So log normal data, obviously, you take the log of log normal data and you're gonna get a normal distribution.
cues.zh: 對數常態資料，顯然對它取對數後，就會得到常態分布。

cues.en: So the point is that, don't look at the slide and say, "Oh, log works better than square root."
cues.zh: 所以重點是，不要看了這張投影片，就說「喔，對數比平方根好」。

cues.en: I could have also generated these data as a power function, and then you would have found that the square root actually works better, brings us closer to a normal distribution
cues.zh: 我也可以用冪函數產生資料，那麼你會發現平方根反而更有效，能比對數更接近

cues.en: then the logarithm.
cues.zh: 常態分布。

cues.en: But you can see both of these functions are pretty similar.
cues.zh: 但可以看到，這兩個函數相當類似。

cues.en: They're both used in cases where you have positive value data, right?
cues.zh: 兩者都用於資料值為正的情況，對吧？

cues.en: You don't want to take the log or the square root of negative numbers.
cues.zh: 你不會想對負數取對數或平方根。

cues.en: So if you have non-negative data and they are right distributed like this, then you can consider taking the log or the square root, and that's going to make the data
cues.zh: 所以，如果資料非負，並且像這樣往右分布，就可以考慮取對數或平方根，這會讓資料

cues.en: approach a normal distribution.
cues.zh: 更接近常態分布。

cues.en: Okay, and then another one that I'll mention here is called Fisher-z.
cues.zh: 接著再提一種，稱為 Fisher-z。

cues.en: Fisher-z transform is for bringing a uniform distribution to a Gaussian-like distribution.
cues.zh: Fisher-z 轉換是用來把均勻分布轉成類似高斯的分布。

cues.en: Now, I haven't yet taught you about the Fisher-z transform in this course, but we will get to it in the section on correlation.
cues.zh: 這門課還沒教 Fisher-z 轉換，但到了相關那一章會談到。

cues.en: That's why you see correlations over here.
cues.zh: 所以這裡會看到相關。

cues.en: This is a screenshot of a slide from the future.
cues.zh: 這是一張來自未來的投影片截圖。

cues.en: I traveled into the future and took this screenshot and then sent it back in time.
cues.zh: 我穿越到未來截了圖，再把它送回過去。

cues.en: So you'll learn about the Fisher-z transform a bit later in the course.
cues.zh: 所以課程稍後會學到 Fisher-z 轉換。

cues.en: Now, as I mentioned, there's many other nonlinear data transformations that depend on the nature of the data.
cues.zh: 如前面所說，還有很多其他非線性資料轉換，要看資料性質。

cues.en: For example, if you have circular data or radiant data, you can take a trig transform.
cues.zh: 例如，如果是圓形資料，或以弧度表示的資料，可以進行三角函數轉換。

cues.en: So you can take the sine and cosine of your circular data, and that will help linearize the data.
cues.zh: 對圓形資料取正弦和餘弦，有助於將資料線性化。

cues.en: Now, on the one hand, applying nonlinear transformations to your data is really easy in the sense that it's really easy just to write the word log in MATLAB or Python.
cues.zh: 一方面，套用非線性轉換非常容易，因為在 MATLAB 或 Python 中寫下 log 這個字很容易。

cues.en: But you do have to be mindful when you are transforming your data using nonlinear methods.
cues.zh: 但使用非線性方法轉換資料時，確實必須留意。

cues.en: So first of all, nonlinear methods are not always appropriate, which I just mentioned in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 首先，非線性方法並不總是適當，這在前一張投影片剛提過。

cues.en: So you have to think carefully about which transformation you are applying and whether that transformation is valid on the data that you're applying it to.
cues.zh: 必須仔細思考使用哪種轉換，以及它對正在處理的資料是否有效。

cues.en: Secondly, nonlinear transformations will actually alter the spacing between data points, and this can vary as a function of the data.
cues.zh: 其次，非線性轉換確實會改變資料點之間的間距，而且可能隨資料而變。

cues.en: So the way that the nonlinear transformation affects the spacing between data points is not necessarily knowable in advance because it might depend on the data.
cues.zh: 所以非線性轉換如何影響資料點間距，不一定事先就能知道，因為可能取決於資料。

cues.en: So one example of how it depends on the data is the rank transform.
cues.zh: 秩轉換就是一個取決於資料的例子。

cues.en: So the spacing, the gap between this number and this number is very small, and the gap between this number and this number is huge.
cues.zh: 這個數字和這個數字之間的間距很小，而這個和這個之間的間距非常大。

cues.en: But here those numbers are of equally close to each other in terms of integers, so we go three and then four and five.
cues.zh: 但這裡的數字以整數來看，彼此間距一樣，所以是 3、4、5。

cues.en: So this is an unpredictable spacing between values that depends on the data themselves.
cues.zh: 這種數值間距的變化無法預先確定，取決於資料本身。

cues.en: Another example is with the log transform.
cues.zh: 另一個例子是對數轉換。

cues.en: So this one is predictable, how it will transform the data, but data values that are very close to each other here that are small, in particular less than one,
cues.zh: 這一種如何轉換資料是可以預測的，但這裡很接近的小數值，特別是小於 1 的數值，

cues.en: so data values that are very close to each other in this range are gonna be further apart from each other in the log transform and the log scale, versus data values that are very close to each other here
cues.zh: 在這個範圍內彼此很接近的資料值，經過對數轉換，在對數尺度上會拉得更開；相反地，這裡彼此很接近的資料值，

cues.en: are really, really close to each other on the log scale.
cues.zh: 在對數尺度上會變得非常非常接近。

cues.en: Now, of course, that is the nature of nonlinear transformations.
cues.zh: 當然，這就是非線性轉換的性質。

cues.en: That is literally built right into the name nonlinear.
cues.zh: 名稱中的「非線性」，本來就直接表達了這一點。

cues.en: So you're gonna have a nonlinear relationship between the spacing of the values in the transform and the spacing of the values in the original data,
cues.zh: 因此，轉換後數值的間距，和原始資料數值的間距，會有非線性關係。

cues.en: but this nonlinearity, this difference in spacing as you go along values of X is important to keep in mind
cues.zh: 但隨著 X 值改變而出現的這種非線性、這種間距差異，必須牢記，

cues.en: because most statistical models are linear.
cues.zh: 因為大多數統計模型是線性的。

cues.en: They're built on linear equations, so that means that the results of linear models have to be interpreted in terms of the transform data, not in terms of the original data.
cues.zh: 它們建立在線性方程式上，所以線性模型結果必須以轉換後的資料來解讀，而不是以原始資料解讀。

cues.en: So let me give you a quick example to make this more concrete.
cues.zh: 快速舉個例子，讓這更具體。

cues.en: Imagine you are investigating the impact of spending more time studying on exam performance.
cues.zh: 假設你在研究多花時間讀書，對考試表現的影響。

cues.en: So here we have our dependent variable here, exam performance, and it goes from zero to 10.
cues.zh: 這裡是依變數，也就是考試表現，範圍從 0 到 10。

cues.en: And let's say you take the log transform of the data and then you find that for every extra hour you spend studying,
cues.zh: 假設對資料取對數，接著發現每多讀一小時，

cues.en: you're going to improve your exam performance by 0.5 points, by half of a point on this scale.
cues.zh: 考試表現就會提升 0.5 分，也就是這個尺度上的半分。

cues.en: Now, if you were to do that in log scale, if you measured the data in logs or transformed the exams by using a log transform, then the impact of studying is actually different
cues.zh: 如果使用對數尺度衡量資料，或者對考試成績進行對數轉換，那麼讀書的影響實際上會不同，

cues.en: depending on your base exam score.
cues.zh: 取決於原本的考試分數。

cues.en: So studying an extra hour is going to help you a lot if you're all the way down here at this end of the exam score, so if you're not doing very well, but if you are doing very well,
cues.zh: 如果考試成績在這裡很低，也就是表現不太好，多讀一小時會有很大幫助；但如果表現很好，

cues.en: then studying for an extra hour isn't actually going to help you that much.
cues.zh: 多讀一小時其實就不會有那麼大幫助。

cues.en: Now on the one hand, that interpretation that I just gave you is pretty interesting, you know, if that's true.
cues.zh: 一方面，剛才給出的解讀相當有趣，假如那是真的。

cues.en: I don't actually know if that's true, although it sounds reasonable.
cues.zh: 我其實不知道是不是真的，雖然聽起來合理。

cues.en: But anyway, I'm just making it up.
cues.zh: 總之，我只是隨意假設。

cues.en: Now that interpretation that I just gave you is fine, but that relies on me taking the result of the statistical model
cues.zh: 剛才這樣解讀沒有問題，但前提是，把統計模型的結果

cues.en: and applying that result back through the transformation, so taking the transformation, the nonlinear transformation in mind.
